issues.legal_issue: A corruption conviction may be sustained on an interested complainant’s testimony when material evidence corroborates the demand and acceptance of the bribe.
material_facts: The complainant testified that the public official demanded money for assistance and later accepted the money during a police trap.
Police officers testified that the official threw the money when the trap party intervened, and the recovered notes matched the numbers recorded before the trap.
A witness to the ride testified to relevant circumstances, and the Supreme Court accepted the evidence of another witness to the seizure.
The discrepancies in the police witnesses’ accounts concerned minor details and did not affect their evidence about the throwing and recovery of the notes.
issues.conclusion: The corroborated evidence was sufficient to sustain the conviction and sentence, so the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: For the offence under Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act read with Section 161 of the Indian Penal Code, an interested complainant’s evidence must be considered with great caution and ordinarily should not be accepted without material corroboration. The Court found corroboration in the other evidence, including the police officers’ account and the matching recovered notes. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.criminal_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.interested_complainant_testified_to_brib: A complainant with an interest in the case testified that the accused demanded or accepted a bribe.
predicates.material_corroboration_supports_bribe: Other material evidence supports the complainant’s account of the bribe demand or acceptance.

issues.definition: When a criminal conviction is appealed, an interested complainant testifies to a bribe, and material evidence corroborates that testimony, the conviction and sentence are upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A witness who is hostile at trial need not have all of their testimony discarded if it still establishes relevant circumstances.
material_facts: The person who drove the vehicle did not support the prosecution’s account in full at trial and differed from an earlier account given to police.
At trial, the driver nevertheless testified to circumstances including that the complainant and the official travelled together and that money was handed over and thrown by the official.
The Court considered the trial testimony as evidence of relevant circumstances while noting that the official’s defence was total denial.
issues.conclusion: The driver’s testimony was not to be discarded altogether and could be considered for the relevant circumstances it established.
issues.legal_principle: A witness’s testimony is not rendered wholly unusable merely because the witness turns hostile; the court may consider the parts of the testimony given in court that it finds relevant and reliable. The judgment refers to the witness’s earlier statement under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure but does not treat that statement as the basis for the ruling. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.criminal_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.hostile_witness_gave_relevant_trial_test: A witness who did not support the prosecution in full at trial nevertheless gave testimony establishing circumstances relevant to the case.

issues.definition: In a criminal conviction appeal, relevant trial testimony is considered even when it comes from a witness who turned hostile.

issues.legal_issue: The non-examination of an attesting witness to a seizure does not undermine a recovery proved by other credible witnesses.
material_facts: An attesting witness to the seizure record was not examined at trial after the prosecutor stated that the witness had been won over.
Police officers testified to the recovery of the currency notes from the vehicle after the official threw them.
The recovered notes matched the numbers recorded before the trap.
issues.conclusion: The non-examination of the attesting witness was not of material consequence because the police officers’ evidence proved the recovery.
issues.legal_principle: The omission to examine an attesting witness is not fatal where other evidence, accepted by the court, establishes the recovery. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this conclusion.

predicates.criminal_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.seizure_attestor_not_examined: A witness who attested a seizure record was not examined at trial.
predicates.recovery_proved_by_other_witnesses: Other witnesses gave evidence establishing the recovery of the seized items.

issues.definition: In a criminal conviction appeal, failure to examine a seizure attestor does not undermine the recovery when other witnesses prove it.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to the authority granting prosecution sanction does not succeed where the record establishes the official’s final allocation to the relevant state service.
material_facts: The appellant argued that the authority granting prosecution sanction lacked power to do so.
A government letter in the record stated that the appellant had been finally allotted to serve as a revenue official in the state.
In light of that letter, counsel did not seriously pursue the challenge.
issues.conclusion: The challenge to the sanctioning authority was of no avail.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the government letter establishing the appellant’s final service allocation and rejected the sanction-authority contention on that basis. The judgment does not identify a specific provision or earlier case as the basis for this conclusion.

predicates.record_supports_official_service_allocat: A document in the record supports that the official was finally allocated to serve in the relevant state service.
